```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Stach 2026 compared the pharmacokinetics of intravenous fentanyl in
anaesthetised male Wistar rats with and without acute fixed-volume hemorrhagic
shock (HS), in which 30% of the estimated blood volume is withdrawn before
dosing. Each group of six rats received 10 ug/kg fentanyl as a 5-min
intravenous infusion, and arterial plasma fentanyl and norfentanyl were
measured by LC-ESI-MS/MS over 60 min.

Fentanyl profiles were analysed in Phoenix WinNonlin 8.2 both by
non-compartmental analysis (Table 2) and by fitting a two-compartment model with
zero-order input and first-order elimination to **each rat individually**
(Table 3). The two groups were fitted separately with the same structure, so
the paper contributes two model files that differ only in their parameter
values:

```{r models}
stach_models <- c(
  "Stach_2026_fentanyl_rat_control", # normovolaemic controls
  "Stach_2026_fentanyl_rat_hemorrhagicShock" # 30% blood-volume withdrawal
)
mod_ctl <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(stach_models[1]))
mod_hs <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(stach_models[2]))
```

* Citation: `r mod_ctl$reference`
* Article: [Eur J Drug Metab Pharmacokinet 2026;51:637-647](https://doi.org/10.1007/s13318-026-01023-z)

```{r description}
for (m in list(mod_ctl, mod_hs)) {
  cat(strwrap(m$description, 76), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}
```

Because the paper reports only the group mean (or median) of the individual
estimates, both files are **typical-value models**: there is no between-animal
variability, and the proportional residual SD implied by the 1/Yhat^2
weighting is fixed at zero. Norfentanyl was characterised only by
non-compartmental analysis (Table 4) and is not modelled.

# Population

```{r population}
pop <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(list(Control = mod_ctl, HS = mod_hs), function(m) {
  p <- m$population
  data.frame(
    Species = p$species, N = p$n_subjects, Age = p$age_range,
    `Body weight` = p$weight_range, Dose = p$dose_range,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}), .id = "Group")
knitr::kable(pop, caption = "Study population (Stach 2026 Methods and Results).")
```

Twelve male Wistar rats aged 18-20 weeks were randomised to a control group or
a fixed-volume HS group (n = 6 each). Both groups were anaesthetised with
isoflurane and catheterised in the jugular vein and femoral artery; in the HS
group 30% of the estimated blood volume (EBV, mL = 0.06 x body weight in g +
0.77) was then withdrawn through the arterial catheter within 15 min, with no
fluid resuscitation. Body weight did not differ between groups (441.3 +/- 26.4
g control, 471.8 +/- 41.1 g HS). At the end of the 60-min study HS animals had
lower albumin (27.8 vs 33.7 g/L) and higher creatinine (61.4 vs 27.1 umol/L)
than controls (Table 1).

# Source trace

| Element | Control | HS | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Structure: 2 compartments, zero-order 5-min input, first-order elimination from central | -- | -- | Methods, Pharmacokinetic Analysis |
| Residual weighting 1/Yhat^2 (proportional), SD not reported -> `propSd` fixed at 0 | 0 | 0 | Results, Compartmental Pharmacokinetics |
| `lcl`: CL (L/h/kg), divided by 60 for the per-minute time base | log(5.9/60) | log(2.6/60) | Table 3, CL |
| `lvc`: Vc (L/kg) | log(0.9) | log(0.6) | Table 3, Vc |
| `lvp`: Vp (L/kg) | log(3.5) | log(3.5) | Table 3, Vp |
| `lq`: Q (L/min/kg), back-solved from median t1/2beta | log(0.1587) | log(0.1700) | Table 3, t1/2beta (44.1 / 78.1 min) |
| Dose 10 ug/kg = 10,000 ng/kg over 5 min | -- | -- | Methods, Experimental Design |
| Concentration = central / Vc; ng/kg / (L/kg) = pg/mL | -- | -- | Units of Tables 2-3 |

## The intercompartmental clearance

Stach 2026 estimated k12 and k21 but Table 3 does not print them. With CL, Vc
and Vp taken from Table 3, the two-compartment system has one free parameter
left, Q. The packaged value of Q makes the beta (elimination) half-life equal
the Table 3 median t1/2beta. The chunk below re-derives it from the table and
checks the implied distribution half-life against the independently reported
t1/2alpha.

```{r q-backsolve}
two_cmt_half_lives <- function(cl, vc, vp, q) {
  k10 <- cl / vc
  k12 <- q / vc
  k21 <- q / vp
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  d <- sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)
  c(alpha = log(2) / ((s + d) / 2), beta = log(2) / ((s - d) / 2))
}
solve_q <- function(cl, vc, vp, target, which) {
  stats::uniroot(
    function(q) two_cmt_half_lives(cl, vc, vp, q)[[which]] - target,
    c(1e-4, 10),
    tol = 1e-10
  )$root
}

table3 <- data.frame(
  group = c("Control", "HS"),
  cl = c(5.9, 2.6) / 60, # L/min/kg
  vc = c(0.9, 0.6),
  vp = c(3.5, 3.5),
  k10 = c(0.12, 0.10), # Table 3 mean K10 (1/min)
  thalf_alpha = c(1.9, 2.4), # Table 3 mean t1/2alpha (min)
  thalf_beta = c(44.1, 78.1) # Table 3 median t1/2beta (min)
)
packaged_q <- c(
  Control = exp(mod_ctl$theta[["lq"]]),
  HS = exp(mod_hs$theta[["lq"]])
)

q_check <- table3 |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    q_from_beta = solve_q(cl, vc, vp, thalf_beta, "beta"),
    q_from_alpha = solve_q(cl, vc, vp, thalf_alpha, "alpha"),
    implied_alpha = two_cmt_half_lives(cl, vc, vp, q_from_beta)[["alpha"]],
    beta_if_alpha_anchor = two_cmt_half_lives(cl, vc, vp, q_from_alpha)[["beta"]],
    k10_from_cl_vc = cl / vc
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(q_packaged = packaged_q[group])

# The packaged Q is the beta-anchored root rounded to 4 significant figures.
stopifnot(all(abs(q_check$q_packaged / q_check$q_from_beta - 1) < 5e-4))

q_check |>
  dplyr::select(
    group, q_packaged, q_from_beta, implied_alpha, thalf_alpha,
    q_from_alpha, beta_if_alpha_anchor, thalf_beta, k10_from_cl_vc, k10
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 4))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Group = group,
    "Q packaged (L/min/kg)" = q_packaged,
    "Q from t1/2beta" = q_from_beta,
    "Implied t1/2alpha (min)" = implied_alpha,
    "Table 3 t1/2alpha (min)" = thalf_alpha,
    "Q from t1/2alpha" = q_from_alpha,
    "t1/2beta if alpha-anchored (min)" = beta_if_alpha_anchor,
    "Table 3 t1/2beta (min)" = thalf_beta,
    "CL/Vc (1/min)" = k10_from_cl_vc,
    "Table 3 K10 (1/min)" = k10
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Back-solving Q from Table 3, and the cross-checks it allows.")
```

The beta-anchored Q gives a distribution half-life of 2.2 min (control) and
1.75 min (HS), both inside one SD of the reported 1.9 +/- 0.7 and 2.4 +/- 0.9
min. Anchoring on t1/2alpha instead would give Q = 0.195 and 0.115 L/min/kg
and a t1/2beta 6% shorter (control) or 8% longer (HS) than reported. The
elimination half-life was chosen as the anchor because the prolonged
elimination is the paper's main finding and is reported as a median, which is
not distorted by the skewed individual estimates.

The Table 3 K10 means (0.12 and 0.10 per min) differ from CL/Vc computed from
the Table 3 CL and Vc means (0.109 and 0.072 per min), because the mean of
individual ratios is not the ratio of the means. CL, Vc and Vp were packaged
because CL is the parameter the paper's conclusions rest on and Vc + Vp
reproduces the reported Vss exactly (4.4 and 4.1 L/kg).

# Virtual cohort

Every parameter is expressed per kg and the dose was weight-normalised
(10 ug/kg), so a single typical rat per group, dosed with 10,000 ng/kg,
represents the whole group; no covariates are needed. The models carry no
between-animal variability, so a stochastic cohort would add nothing.

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
dose_ng_per_kg <- 10000 # 10 ug/kg
t_inf <- 5 # min

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 60, by = 0.5), seq(61, 900, by = 1))))
ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_ng_per_kg, dur = t_inf, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(obs_times, cmt = "central")

sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ctl, ev)) |> dplyr::mutate(group = "Control"),
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_hs, ev)) |> dplyr::mutate(group = "HS")
) |>
  dplyr::select(group, time, Cc)
```

## Figure 1A: fentanyl plasma concentrations

```{r fig1a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1A of Stach 2026. Lines: typical-value simulations. Points: group means read approximately from the published figure by the maintainers (log axis, so roughly +/-10%)."}
fig1a_means <- data.frame(
  group = rep(c("Control", "HS"), each = 8),
  time = rep(c(5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60), 2),
  Cc = c(
    6000, 1800, 1230, 930, 870, 650, 480, 520,
    13000, 2950, 1950, 1480, 1100, 990, 860, 1000
  )
)

ggplot(dplyr::filter(sim, time != 0, time <= 60), aes(time, Cc, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig1a_means, size = 2) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(100, 1e5)) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Fentanyl plasma concentration (pg/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

The typical-value curves follow the published means from 10 min onwards. At the
end of the infusion (5 min) the HS model sits below the published mean of about
13,000 pg/mL; the HS group had the most variable peak concentrations (Table 2
median 13,060, interquartile range 7,785-13,820 pg/mL), and a typical-value
model built from the mean Vc cannot reproduce the mean of a skewed set of
individual peaks.

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
nca_input <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L)
stopifnot(all(tapply(nca_input$time, nca_input$group, min) == 0))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_input, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  data.frame(
    group = c("Control", "HS"), id = 1L, time = 0,
    amt = dose_ng_per_kg, duration = t_inf
  ),
  amt ~ time | group + id,
  duration = "duration",
  route = "intravascular"
)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 5), end = c(Inf, 60),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE), aucinf.obs = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  half.life = c(TRUE, FALSE), cl.obs = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published values

Reference values are the Table 3 compartmental summaries (Cmax and t1/2beta as
medians, AUC0-inf and CL as means) and the Table 2 non-compartmental AUC0-t.
CL is converted to L/min/kg.

The Table 2 "AUC0-t" does not include the infusion period. The linear
trapezoidal area under the Figure 1A group means reproduces it only when the
area starts at the first sample (5 min), not at the start of the infusion:

```{r auct-identity}
trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
fig1a_means |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc_5_60 = trap(time, Cc),
    auc_0_60 = trap(c(0, time), c(0, Cc))
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(table2_auc0t = c(59675, 102163)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Group = group,
    "Figure 1A means, 5-60 min" = auc_5_60,
    "Figure 1A means, 0-60 min" = auc_0_60,
    "Table 2 AUC0-t" = table2_auc0t
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Trapezoidal AUC (min pg/mL) of the approximate Figure 1A means.")
```

The simulated counterpart is therefore the area from 5 to 60 min (auclast over
the 5-60 min interval below).

```{r nca-compare}
published_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,    ~PPTESTCD,    ~PPORRES,
  "Control", "cmax",          4589,      # Table 3, median
  "Control", "aucinf.obs",  104357,      # Table 3, mean
  "Control", "half.life",     44.1,      # Table 3, median t1/2beta
  "Control", "cl.obs",       5.9 / 60,   # Table 3, mean CL
  "Control", "auclast",      59675,      # Table 2, mean AUC0-t
  "HS",      "cmax",         10091,      # Table 3, median
  "HS",      "aucinf.obs",  242210,      # Table 3, mean
  "HS",      "half.life",     78.1,      # Table 3, median t1/2beta
  "HS",      "cl.obs",       2.6 / 60,   # Table 3, mean CL
  "HS",      "auclast",     102163       # Table 2, mean AUC0-t
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "group",
  params = c("cmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cl.obs"),
  units = c(
    cmax = "pg/mL", auclast = "min pg/mL", aucinf.obs = "min pg/mL",
    half.life = "min", cl.obs = "L/min/kg"
  ),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "Simulated typical-value NCA versus Stach 2026 Tables 2 and 3.",
  "* marks a difference above 20%. AUClast is the area from 5 to 60 min, compared",
  "with the Table 2 AUC0-t (see above)."
))
```

```{r nca-assert}
sim_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cl.obs")) |>
  dplyr::select(group, PPTESTCD, sim = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published_nca, by = c("group", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (sim / PPORRES - 1))
# Deterministic typical-value solves. CL and AUC0-inf are a direct read of the
# packaged CL (AUC = Dose / CL), so they sit within a few percent of the
# Table 3 means; the terminal half-life reproduces the median t1/2beta that Q
# was anchored on.
stopifnot(
  nrow(sim_wide) == 6,
  all(abs(sim_wide$pct[sim_wide$PPTESTCD == "cl.obs"]) < 10),
  all(abs(sim_wide$pct[sim_wide$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"]) < 10),
  all(abs(sim_wide$pct[sim_wide$PPTESTCD == "half.life"]) < 5)
)
```

The model reproduces the exposure-driving parameters of both groups:
AUC0-inf = Dose/CL lies 3-5% below the Table 3 means (a typical animal is
expected to sit slightly below the mean of individual AUCs, which are
right-skewed), and the terminal half-life matches the reported medians by
construction. The area over the sampled window (5-60 min), which depends on all
four parameters and was not used to build the model, lies 8% (control) and 13%
(HS) below the observed non-compartmental AUC0-t.

Cmax is the one parameter that differs by more than 20% in the control group.
Cmax in a 5-min infusion depends almost entirely on Vc and on the fast
distribution phase, and Vc is the least precisely known parameter in Table 3
(SD 0.4 L/kg on means of 0.9 and 0.6 L/kg). The typical-value peak (computed
from the mean Vc) is therefore not expected to equal the median of the six
individual peaks; the control-group simulation (about 6,100 pg/mL) does agree
with the mean of about 6,000 pg/mL in Figure 1A.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Two-stage summaries packaged as typical values.** Table 3 reports the mean
  (or median) of six individual WinNonlin fits per group. CL, Vc and Vp are
  the group means; no between-animal variability is encoded because the
  standard deviations of individual estimates include estimation error and are
  not population variance estimates.
* **Q back-solved.** The intercompartmental rate constants k12 and k21 were
  estimated but not reported. Q was solved so the beta half-life equals the
  Table 3 median t1/2beta (see the back-solve table above); the alternative
  alpha-anchored values are shown there for comparison.
* **K10 not used.** The Table 3 mean K10 is inconsistent with CL/Vc from the
  table means (0.12 vs 0.109 per min control, 0.10 vs 0.072 per min HS);
  CL and Vc were retained.
* **Time base.** The models run in minutes. Table 3 reports CL in L/h/kg; it
  was divided by 60. Time zero is the start of the 5-min infusion, matching
  the paper's non-compartmental Vss formula `CL x (MRT - Tinf/2)` and the
  first sample at 5 min.
* **Residual error.** The 1/Yhat^2 weighting implies a proportional error model;
  its magnitude was not reported, so `propSd` is fixed at 0.
* **Group as two files.** HS is not a covariate in the paper; the two groups
  were fitted separately with the same structure, so each is its own model
  file.
* **Not modelled.** Norfentanyl (non-compartmental only, Table 4; metabolic
  conversion ratio 0.197 control vs 0.117 HS) and the plasma biochemistry
  (Table 1).
* **Table 2 AUC0-t starts at 5 min.** Its values match the trapezoidal area of
  the Figure 1A means from the first sample (5 min) to 60 min and are about 20%
  (control) and 25% (HS) below the area from the start of the infusion, so they
  are compared with a simulated AUC over 5-60 min. The Table 2 AUC0-inf, CL and
  t1/2lambdaz, which build on that area, were not used as comparison targets.
* **Figure points.** The Figure 1A means plotted above were read from the
  published figure by eye and are approximate; they are used for display and
  for the AUC0-t check, not for any assertion.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found in Europe PMC for this
  article as of 2026-11-17.
